Botnet_ARES.description: Traffic from compromised devices controlled remotely by an attacker, often an IoT botnet using encrypted communication.
mitigation: Keep smart/IoT devices updated and change their default usernames and passwords.
Put smart/IoT devices on a separate Wi-Fi or network from work computers.
Watch for devices contacting strange addresses or checking in regularly; ask your ISP or IT provider if unsure.

DDoS_LOIT.description: Distributed denial-of-service attack using the Low Orbit Ion Cannon tool to flood a target with TCP, UDP, or HTTP requests.
mitigation: Use a service from your hosting provider or ISP that filters attack traffic.
Limit how many connections or requests each IP address can make at your network edge; ask hosting/IT to set this up.
Turn on server protections against connection floods, such as SYN cookies, and set connection limits.

DoS_GoldenEye.description: Single-source denial-of-service attack using the GoldenEye tool, often sending HTTP GET/POST floods and slow-connection attacks.
mitigation: Put a website security filter (web application firewall) in front with rules that limit repeated requests.
Set short timeouts so slow connections do not tie up the server.
Use a load balancer or hosting service that can handle sudden traffic bursts.

DoS_Hulk.description: High-volume HTTP flood attack that overwhelms a web server with many unique or obfuscated requests.
mitigation: Limit how many requests each IP address can make.
Use a website security filter (web application firewall) to block repeated or malformed requests.
Set up automatic scaling or ask your hosting provider to absorb traffic spikes.

DoS_Slowhttptest.description: Slow denial-of-service attack that keeps many connections open by sending HTTP headers very slowly, exhausting server connection pools.
mitigation: Reduce how long the server waits for slow clients and cap the maximum number of connections.
Put a reverse proxy in front of the server to buffer slow clients.
Set up alerts for many unfinished HTTP requests.

DoS_Slowloris.description: Slow denial-of-service attack that opens many connections and sends partial HTTP headers slowly, blocking legitimate users.
mitigation: Configure the web server to close idle or slow connections quickly.
Limit how many connections one IP address can open at the same time.
Use a website security filter or load balancer with slow-attack protection.

FTP-Patator.description: Brute-force attack that repeatedly tries username/password combinations against an FTP service.
mitigation: Require strong passwords and lock accounts after several failed login attempts.
Turn off FTP if it is not needed; use SFTP or FTPS instead.
Check FTP logs for many failed login attempts.

Heartbleed.description: Exploitation of the Heartbleed bug in OpenSSL to read sensitive server memory, including private keys.
mitigation: Update or patch OpenSSL right away.
Replace SSL certificates and private keys that may have been exposed.
Run a vulnerability scan to confirm no unpatched services remain.

Port_Scan.description: Automated scanning of a network to discover open ports and running services, often a precursor to an attack.
mitigation: Use a firewall to block unrequested incoming connections.
Use an intrusion-detection system that alerts on many port probes.
Close ports and services that are not needed on all devices.

SSH-Patator.description: Brute-force attack against SSH login, trying many username/password pairs to break into a system.
mitigation: Turn off password-based SSH login and use SSH keys instead.
Move SSH off the default port 22 as a small deterrent.
Use fail2ban or a similar tool to block IPs after repeated failed logins.

Web_Brute_Force.description: Automated guessing of login credentials on a web application authentication form.
mitigation: Add CAPTCHA or rate limits to login pages.
Lock accounts after a small number of failed login attempts.
Turn on multi-factor authentication for user accounts.

Web_SQL_Injection.description: Attacker inserts malicious SQL code into input fields to manipulate or extract data from a backend database.
mitigation: Use safe database queries, such as parameterised queries or prepared statements; ask your developer to confirm.
Check and clean all user input on the server side.
Use a website security filter with SQL-injection rules and run vulnerability scans.

Web_XSS.description: Cross-site scripting attack where malicious JavaScript is injected into a web page and executed in other users' browsers.
mitigation: Encode output and validate input to prevent script injection.
Add a Content-Security-Policy header; ask your hosting provider or developer for help.
Keep web frameworks and libraries updated, and use a website security filter to block common XSS patterns.
